thread:
monitor-bot: [ALERT] PAGER: Elevated 5xx and connection timeouts detected for services egressing through az-p-nat-1 (az-p-north-1a/1b). Spike started ~2330102000. Net oncall paged.

oncall-net: ack — jumping in. Is there visible customer impact?

maria: seeing a bunch of 504s from our edge -> internal services. NAT gateway metrics show SNAT port pressure; conntrack drops on nat instances.

alex: checking VPC flow logs now — large spike in ephemeral port usage. Any recent infra changes in az-p?

jules: infra: I ran an automated NACL cleanup job ~20m ago that reapplied NACLs across prod AZs. No manual SG changes that I know of.

opsbot: Deploy bot: infra/cleanup terraform apply finished at 2330101000 (user: infra-maintainer). Summary: reapplied prod NACLs in az-p.

maria: that could be it — if the NACL template accidentally tightened ephemeral port range we'd see SNAT exhaustion. Pulling current NACL rules.

alex: can someone run conntrack stats on the nat instance? Command: `sudo conntrack -S` and `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l`.

jules: conntrack dump snippet pasted: 
```
conntrack entries: 65535
packets: ...
drops: 4321
```

support-desk: Customer impact: multiple timeouts reported for embedding/ML API proxied via az-p; ticket count increasing. Slack thread from customer ops showing elevated 504s.

maria: NAT GW cloud metrics show ephemeral_port_high_watermark reached. Looks consistent with ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT instances.

alex: mitigation options: 1) add NAT capacity (new nat-instance or secondary NAT GW) and shift route table association 2) revert NACL change if it's blocking ephemeral range 3) as last resort flush conntrack on nat instances (will break existing conns).

oncall-net: prioritize non-disruptive: spin up standby nat-instance and shift some private subnets to it, then revert NACL. Who can run the standby launch?

jules: I'll kick off the standby. Using bootstrap script.

opsbot: Command suggestion: 
```
./scripts/one-off/nat-standby-launch.sh --az az-p-north-1a --size t3.medium
```
(I can execute if given confirmation).

maria: Also prepping a conntrack flush if we need immediate relief: `sudo conntrack -F` — warning: will drop active connections.

alex: prefer adding capacity first to avoid causing additional customer disruption.

jules: nat-standby launched; EIP attached; updating route table for private subnet 10.20.0.0/16 to use nat-instance-standby. Monitoring shift now.

monitor-bot: Route table change detected (rtb-azp-priv-10-20) — association updated at 2330103200.

support-desk: Early signals: reduction in 504s and ticket inflow slowing. Customers reporting partial recovery.

maria: running connectivity tests from private subnet — embedding endpoint responses now succeed from multiple test hosts. Conntrack drops trending down from 4321 -> ~200.

oncall-net: can we identify the offending NACL rule? If it's a template issue we should revert and patch infra job.

jules: found it: NACL acl-0x9c had a deny for ephemeral outbound ports due to a bad template entry (32768-65535 denied). Reverting to allow outbound ephemeral range now.

opsbot: NACL revert applied at 2330103800.

maria: after revert, conntrack drops down to single digits, latencies normalized, and customer 5xx rate back to baseline.

alex: follow-ups: 1) add preflight check in infra cleanup to detect ephemeral port denies 2) add safety flag to skip NACL changes for production subnets 3) consider autoscaling NAT capacity or add standby pool to avoid manual launches.

oncall-net: agree. Also recommend an automated alert for ephemeral_port_high_watermark earlier in the pipeline.

support-desk: customer comms: "We identified a NAT SNAT port exhaustion caused by an automated NACL reapply which inadvertently blocked ephemeral outbound ports. We restored normal traffic by rolling standby NAT capacity and reverting the NACL. A postmortem will follow." Customers acknowledged.

maria: filing uptask: infra cleanup preflight + NACL guardrails. Assigning to @alex and @jules for PR review.

jules: handing over to day oncall — @kevin you're up for the post-incident follow-up and postmortem. I'll add runbook notes in the pager duty incident.

oncall-net: handoff acknowledged — leaving thread. Great run team :thumbsup: 

monitor-bot: Incident condition resolved — system metrics stable for 15m. If recurrence detected reopen.
